easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the godly man ceaseth.”
easy.q: What kind of man is said to cease?

easy.explanation: The verse says the faithful fail “from among the children of men.”
easy.q: Among whom do the faithful fail?

answers: Comes to an end or disappears
medium.explanation: “Ceaseth” means stops or is no longer present.
medium.q: What does “ceaseth” mean in this verse?

medium.explanation: The wording indicates that faithful people are no longer common.

answers: The decline of godly and faithful people
The loss of a musical instrument
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for help because godly and faithful people are disappearing.
medium.q: What is the main concern expressed in the verse?

answers: The psalmist asks for divine help because faithfulness is disappearing
The psalmist asks for music because the temple is empty
The psalmist asks for wealth because the poor are prosperous
challenge.explanation: The plea for help responds to the shortage of godly and faithful people.
challenge.q: How does the opening plea relate to the condition described afterward?

answers: Godliness is presented as rare among humanity
All humanity is described as perfectly godly
The verse contrasts musicians with soldiers
challenge.explanation: The verse portrays godliness and faithfulness as scarce among people.
challenge.q: What contrast is implied by “the godly man” and “the children of men”?

answers: A prayer for help amid moral and spiritual decline
A description of a musical performance
challenge.explanation: The verse is a plea for help because faithful people are failing.
challenge.q: Which summary best matches the verse?

paragraphs.title: The Disappearance of Trust and the Rise of Deceptive Speech

easy.explanation: The verse says, “They speak vanity every one with his neighbour.”
easy.q: What do people speak to one another?
What kind of lips do they have?
What do they have when they speak?

medium.explanation: Here “vanity” refers to empty, false, or worthless words.
medium.q: What does “vanity” mean in this context?

answers: Speech that pleases or praises deceptively
medium.explanation: Flattery uses pleasing words, often without honest motives.
A double heart indicates that outward speech and inward motives do not agree.

answers: Smooth speech hides divided or dishonest motives
The two phrases describe physical illness
challenge.explanation: The passage connects deceptive praise with insincerity.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between flattering lips and a double heart?

answers: Trust has weakened because speech is false and insincere
Trust has increased through truthful speech
challenge.explanation: False words, flattery, and divided motives undermine trust.
challenge.q: What does the passage suggest about trust among the people?

answers: People use persuasive speech without honest hearts
People refuse to speak at all
People use music to comfort the needy
challenge.explanation: The passage focuses on deceptive speech and proud words used for selfish purposes.
challenge.q: Which statement best captures the danger described in verses 2–5?

paragraphs.title: God’s Response and Protection of the Oppressed

answers: Because of the oppression of the poor and the sighing of the needy
easy.explanation: The LORD responds to the oppression of the poor and the sighing of the needy.
easy.q: Why does the LORD say He will arise?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will set him in safety.”
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to do for the afflicted?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “The words of the LORD are pure words.”
easy.q: How are the words of the LORD described?

medium.explanation: The needy are people in hardship who require assistance.
They are compared to silver purified in a furnace.
medium.q: What are the LORD’s words compared to?

answers: The truth and perfection of God’s words
medium.explanation: Refined silver illustrates purity and reliability.
medium.q: What does the comparison with purified silver emphasize?

answers: Human speech is deceptive, while the LORD’s words are pure
Both are described as equally false
Human speech is pure, while the LORD’s words are flattering
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts deceptive human speech with God’s purified words.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between human speech and the LORD’s words?

challenge.explanation: “For ever” emphasizes the continuing nature of the LORD’s preservation.
challenge.q: What does “preserve them from this generation for ever” communicate?

answers: God promises pure speech, safety, and preservation amid human deceit
God abandons the oppressed to the wicked
challenge.explanation: God answers human corruption with His pure word and protection.
challenge.q: How do verses 6–8 answer the crisis in verses 2–5?

paragraphs.title: The Continued Presence of the Wicked

easy.explanation: The closing line says, “The wicked walk on every side.”

answers: The wicked continue to surround others
easy.explanation: The line presents the wicked as active while vile men are elevated.
easy.q: What happens when the vilest men are exalted?

easy.explanation: The verse refers to “the vilest men.”
easy.q: Which group is described as being exalted?

answers: The wicked are widespread and active
The wicked are confined to one place
medium.explanation: The phrase suggests broad and continuing presence.
medium.q: What does “walk on every side” suggest?

medium.explanation: “Vilest” refers to people regarded as especially base or wicked.

answers: Bad people are elevated while wickedness remains widespread
The poor are safely protected from every danger
medium.explanation: The line depicts the exaltation of vile people and the continuing presence of the wicked.
medium.q: What troubling condition is shown in the closing line?

answers: Divine protection is promised, yet wickedness is still visible in the world
The LORD’s words are shown to be false
The poor are said to oppress the wicked
challenge.explanation: The closing line acknowledges that wickedness continues despite God’s promise.
challenge.q: What tension remains after the LORD promises preservation?

answers: It recognizes that corruption remains a present reality
It changes the psalm into a celebration of the wicked
It removes the need for divine help
challenge.explanation: The ending keeps attention on the continuing reality of moral corruption.
challenge.q: How does the final image affect the psalm’s overall message?

answers: The wicked are widespread, and contemptible people are being raised up
The wicked are protecting the faithful, and the poor are exalted
The wicked have vanished, and righteousness rules everywhere
challenge.explanation: Both clauses describe the prominence of wickedness and vile people.
challenge.q: Which interpretation best connects the two parts of the closing line?
